q: According to the Bergonie-Tribondeau law, rapidly dividing undifferentiated cells are the most radiosensitive. Of these options, the most radiosensitive cell is:
ex: Spermatogonia divide rapidly and are among the most radiosensitive cells in the body.

q: A radiographer working at distance d from a point photon source steps back to distance 2d. The exposure rate at the new spot relative to the original rate follows which rule:
ex: A point-source beam follows the inverse-square law; doubling distance quarters the exposure rate.

q: Routine personal dose monitoring of diagnostic radiology staff in India today uses which of the following devices?
ex: TLD badges have replaced film badges for individual dose records of staff.

q: Which agent first introduced non-ionic water-soluble contrast into clinical practice?
ex: Metrizamide was the first non-ionic contrast agent; diatrizoate is an older ionic agent.

q: A patient with eGFR of 35 ml per minute needs iodinated contrast. Which of the following carries the lowest risk of contrast-induced nephropathy?
ex: Iodixanol, an iso-osmolar non-ionic dimer, carries the lowest CIN risk among iodinated agents.

q: In a patient with advanced renal failure needing MRI, which agent minimises the risk of nephrogenic systemic fibrosis?
o: Linear chelate of the ligand first-gen
ex: Macrocyclic chelates release far less free gadolinium and carry the lowest NSF risk.

q: The ground-glass granular film of a premature newborn with air bronchograms and overinflation suggests:
ex: RDS shows ground-glass granularity with air bronchograms; TTNB differs.

q: On a supine film of the newborn with free intra-peritoneal air, the gas under the whole abdominal wall drawing an oval silhouette is the:
ex: The oval air outline of the whole peritoneal cavity on the supine film is the football sign.

q: A newborn with delayed meconium who shows a narrowed distal rectal segment with an abrupt transition cone on the enema has:
ex: An aganglionic spastic distal segment with a transition cone on enema is Hirschsprung disease.

q: A newborn with foamy granular opacities in the right upper abdomen and a colon of normal calibre has a suspicion of meconium ileus. The best next investigation is:
ex: Water-soluble contrast enema both diagnoses and treats meconium ileus; cystic fibrosis underlies most.

q: The triangular opacity hugging the right upper mediastinum on a normal newborn chest film that changes shape with crying is:
ex: The sail sign is the normal thymus of infancy that shifts with posture and cry.

q: A patient lucid for a while after a head hit then comatose with a biconvex lentiform bleed that does not cross a suture on NCCT:
ex: Classic extradural haematoma: lucid interval, biconvex, sutures respected.

q: Fall of a week before in an elderly anticoagulated patient with confusion and a crescent of fluid over a convexity of the brain: choose the decisive next step.
ex: Concave crescentic subacute subdural causes mental change; burr hole evacuation is definitive.

q: A patient 90 minutes after a hemiplegic stroke has a practically normal plain CT. Which MRI sequence shows the acute infarct?
ex: DWI shows cytotoxic oedema within minutes and is the most sensitive acute-stroke sequence.

q: Sudden thunderclap headache and stiff neck: the cerebral cisterns run bright on non-enhanced CT. The entity is:
ex: Left fissural hyperdensity of blood in cisterns is the signature of acute SAH.

q: A febrile patient with seizures has an MRI ring-enhancing lesion with its core bright on the diffusion sequence. The likeliest diagnosis is:
ex: Pus restricts diffusion, so an abscess ring-enhances but shines bright on DWI, unlike necrotic tumour.

q: MRI shows an expansive sella mass rising out to the suprasellar with a snowman waist pressing on the optic chiasm. Diagnosis:
ex: A snowman-shaped sellar suprasellar mass with chiasmal compression is a pituitary macroadenoma.

q: Enhancing dural-based mass with a broad base and hyperostosis of the adjacent skull vault on CT is most likely:
ex: Uniformly enhancing extra-axial lesion on the dura with hyperostosis is a meningioma.

q: A PA chest film shows a convex pulmonary artery segment and right hilar prominence in a breathless young patient. This picture is most consistent with:
ex: A convex main PA segment and full lung vessels reflect shunt or pulmonary hypertension.

q: A good suspected ferromagnetic intraocular foreign body after chisel injury; which test must be avoided lest the metallic piece move?
ex: MRI torque a ferromagnetic intraocular FB; plain films and CT are the safe detection route.

q: Expansion of an opaque frontal sinus with a thin intact frame seen over weeks of frontal headache is:
ex: A mucocoele is an expanded paranasal sinus under obstruction which slowly erodes it.

q: Dysphonia, inferior of the hill, and an apical mass in a long smoker with rib pitting the first-two ribs: the diagnosis is:
ex: The superior sulcus (Pancoast) tumour induces rib destruction, Horner and a brachial ache.

q: The child murmur with a film where the pulmonary cripples are engorged and the oxygen zones appear dense (plethoric fields) most likely has:
ex: Left-to-right shunts overload the pulmonary bed and give plethoric lung fields, cyanotic shunts the opposite.

q: PA film with an enlarged left atrial apage sickle and elevation of the left main bronchus in a patient with chest-murmur indicates:
ex: Left atrial growth bulges the appendage, raises the left main bronchus and indents the barium column.

q: A dilated oesophagus that ends in a smooth taper at the cardia and empties slowly on a swallow; what is the diagnosis?
ex: Smooth beak narrowing at the cardia with upstream dilatation is achalasia.

q: Barium in young adult with low-grade fever and abdominal discomfort shows an ileocaecal stricture, the caecum distorted, and a fleck. Suspect:
ex: Contractile ileocaecal-TB is the goblet caecum fleck lead in a young Indian adult.

q: A 3-month-old who healthy a projectile feed film shows a muscle thickness of 4 mm and an elongated playtrap. Diagnosis:
ex: Pyloric muscle wall thickness over 3-4 mm and a long canal confirm hypertrophic pyloric stenosis.

q: In the blunt abdd child the supine film has no free gas; the most sensitive view for bowel perforation is:
ex: Erect and decubitus films collect free gas under the diaphragm that supine film misses.

q: Guggling, lumpy swallowing with regurgitation of a previous meal; a pouch high behind the cricoid fills. The lesion is:
ex: The Zenker pouch is a hypopharynxoutpouching above the cricopharynges that returns retained food.

q: Obstruction with gaseous lucencies over liver and a calcified concretion lodged in a distal small loop on the same film to represent the:
ex: Pneumobilia over the liver plus an obstructing ectopic stone is the Rigler triad of gallstone ileus.

q: A skip in the cyst of proximal humerus of a limping adolescent with a soap-bubble blow-out and thin cortices: with the diagnosis?
ex: Multicysticated soap-bubble expansile metaphyseal lesion of the young stands for an aneurysmal bone cyst.

q: The frog-lateral shows a femoral head-piece slip from the neck in a growing thigh. This is:
ex: An adolescent medial slip of the epiphysis on frog-lat is SCFE.

q: A lytic focus in the distal femoral epiphysis with specks of matrix in a teen's knee:
ex: Lucent epiphyseal crest in the young with flecks of chondroid is a chondroblastoma.

q: Longbone sprorrow pointing away from the joint with cortex and marrow continuous with the host; this is:
ex: The sessile or pedunculate exostosis has marrow continu with the mother bone.

q: 70-year pain after a trivial fall with a pelvis nuclear scan that draws an 'H' over the sacral & hips:
ex: Honda sign, an H-shaped tracer band over both sacral alae, is insufficiency sacral fracture.

q: In a stable film of a burning knee is a curved dense line over the bone tip of a menopause woman: crystal is:
ex: Chondrocalcinosis with fibrocartilage-calcified lines is the CPPD of pseudo-gout.

q: Ligature with ascending rigidity and a single-shot lateral of the entire spine full of continuous bridges:
ex: Vertebral syndesmophryte bridging (bamboo spine) is ankylosing spondylitis.

q: Kidney film shows a branched stag-horn shadow reproducing the whole pelvicalyceal pattern after repeated urinary infections: the stone is:
ex: Staghorn replica of a pelvicalyceal cast on an infected urine meets struvite stone chemistry.

q: A booked colic emergency: the ideal single test that shows the site and size of the obstrpellet effect at:
o: Unenhanced CT of the urinary tract
ex: Unenhanced CT exam scan for calculi is the best emergency modality.

q: In a child with recurrent infective voiding, the study that confirms the reflux into a ureter while he voids is:
ex: Micturating cytogram shows the vestibular reflux that fills it during curl.

q: A bulky redundant renal pelvis with a narrowed fleure at the pelvic side of a kidney in a young adult points to:
ex: PUJ obstruction is suggested of the calyx atrium and the whole pelvis.

q: Fluid-space with intraluminal folded tape in the liver that hangs in the cyst like a thread: which sign is this?
ex: The water-lily sign is the folded ruptated endocyst of hydatid disease in the liver.

q: Hypertension in youth with a short segment of rigid string-of-globe in the middle renal artery on an angiogram:
ex: Multifocal beading of a renal artery in a young hypertensive is fibromuscular dysplasia.

q: Young hypoxic adult with a oligaemic opacity and a flattened Westermark: alongside a large PA, the association to recall is:
ex: The Westermark sign (oligaemia; sharp blood) sits in pulmonary embolism.

q: The shrill ring of calcified egg crust in both hila of a foundry worker who sweeps:
ex: Peripheral egg-shell hilar node calcification is the silicosis classic.

q: A renal carcinoma that mostly produces painless litre's oll and hypertension has several micro-aneurysms in a mycoma: the angiographic hallmark is:
ex: Stippled beaded tumour vessels drawing venous corkscrews mark the renal cancer angiogram.
